data.title: Initial Level Placement
data.description: A high-level scan to establish your current CEFR baseline (A2-B2).

sections.explain: We normally say 'make a decision', not 'do' or 'take' a decision in standard everyday English.

words.word: We need to make a decision before Friday.
We need to do a decision before Friday.
We need to create a decision before Friday.

sections.explain: 'Lend' means to give something temporarily; 'borrow' means to receive it temporarily.

words.word: Could you borrow me your charger for an hour?
Could you lend me your charger for an hour?
Could you owe me your charger for an hour?

sections.sentence: Choose the adjective that describes the person's feeling.
sections.explain: 'Disappointed' describes how a person feels; 'disappointing' describes the thing that causes the feeling.

words.word: She was disappointing when the concert was cancelled.
She was disappointment when the concert was cancelled.
She was disappointed when the concert was cancelled.

sections.explain: The standard collocation is 'take responsibility for' something.

words.word: He refused to take responsibility for the mistake.
He refused to make responsibility for the mistake.
He refused to carry responsibility of the mistake.

sections.sentence: Choose the phrasal verb that means 'have none left'.
sections.explain: 'Run out of' means to use all of something so that none remains.

words.word: We have turned out of milk.
We have run out of milk.
We have broken out of milk.

sections.explain: 'Affect' is normally a verb meaning to influence. 'Effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

words.word: The new timetable will effect how often the buses run.
The new timetable will result how often the buses run.
The new timetable will affect how often the buses run.

sections.sentence: Choose the word meaning practical and reasonable.
sections.explain: 'Sensible' means practical or showing good judgement. 'Sensitive' means easily affected or aware of feelings.

words.word: Taking a coat was a sensible decision because it was cold.
Taking a coat was a sensitive decision because it was cold.
Taking a coat was a sympathetic decision because it was cold.

sections.summary: B1 Lexis: Adverb and Adjective Collocations.
sections.explain: 'Highly unlikely' is a common collocation meaning very improbable.

words.word: It is deeply unlikely that the match will continue.
It is highly unlikely that the match will continue.
It is loudly unlikely that the match will continue.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct verb for introducing a topic or concern.
sections.explain: We 'raise an issue' when we introduce it for discussion.

words.word: Several staff raised the issue at the meeting.
Several staff lifted the issue at the meeting.
Several staff increased the issue at the meeting.

sections.sentence: Choose the sentence in which 'eventually' is used correctly.
sections.summary: B1 Lexis: False Friends and Time Adverbs.
sections.explain: 'Eventually' means 'in the end, after some time', not 'possibly' or 'at the present time'.

words.word: Eventually, I am working from home today.
The journey was difficult, but we eventually arrived.
It will eventually rain tomorrow, but I am not sure.
